corpus.design: T1 instruction override, T2 tool-choice coercion, T3 exfiltration sink, T4 persona hijack, T5 memory carryover (cross-session), T6 canary leak (label betrayal); B1 customer reply, B2 HR-to-HR, B3 forum reply, B4 clean memory then privileged batch

latency.methodology: in-process hot loop, 4000 sessions × 6-decision representative mix (glob read, delta read, gated egress with canary scan, ledger write, ledger join, trust-floor denial)

appaBaseline.label: APPA-baseline mirror (TS engine, organs off — session-scoped labels)
appaBaseline.provenance: prototype measurement — ours (semantic mirror of the real binary)

latency.methodology: in-process hot loop, 4000 sessions × 6-decision representative mix (glob read, delta read, gated egress with canary scan, ledger write, ledger join, trust-floor denial)

appaBlunt.label: APPA + blunt memory annotation
appaBlunt.provenance: prototype measurement — ours (TS mirror) + real binary run
appaBlunt.note: same policy with mcp/memory/read annotated delta={trust:"suspicious"} — closes T5 but breaks every benign privileged memory flow (B4)

openappa.label: OpenAPPA v0.30.0 (real binary, replay mode, base policy)
openappa.provenance: prototype measurement — real MIT binary, our corpus

latency.methodology: per-step cost amortized over a 40-step session-scale trace (7 runs, min) — the replay CLI scales superlinearly with trace length, so long-session per-step costs are higher; per-session cost = mean wall time of single-scenario replay invocations (includes process startup). The replay CLI is OpenAPPA’s offline validation mode, not necessarily its production hot path.

regex.label: Regex/DLP blocklist (10 patterns, locked before measuring)

latency.methodology: in-process hot loop over all 40 corpus narratives, 300 passes

llmJudge.label: LLM-as-judge guardrail (hosted LLM)

latency.methodology: wall-clock per judged scenario, incl. network and model time; one call each (retries only on parse/rate-limit failure); latencies measured on the first full pass; latency figures from the measured full pass of 2026-10-02 (same harness, same model); accuracy re-confirmed fresh 2026-10-04

llmJudge.caveat: single-run, non-deterministic; a strong judge is accurate on informative narratives — the deterministic advantage is reproducibility, auditability, and ~3–4 orders of magnitude lower latency

findings: The real OpenAPPA binary reproduces the whitepaper’s in-session claim on this corpus: T1–T4 (classic injection, coercion, exfil, hijack) blocked 16/16, benign 16/16.

The same binary confirms the two structural blind spots the whitepaper flags: T5 memory carryover 0/4 and T6 label betrayal 0/4 — poison persisted in durable memory re-enters a fresh session unscarred; mislabeled content sails through label-only gates.
The strongest blunt patch an operator can write without foreknowledge of attacker-chosen keys (memory/read annotated suspicious) closes T5 4/4 but kills B4 0/4 — blind or blunt, not precise.
PANOPTES’ organs close both gaps at no benign cost on this corpus: ledger join (T5 4/4), canary interdiction (T6 4/4), B4 intact — at comparable per-decision cost to the label-only fast path.
The LLM judge got 100%/100% on this corpus in one run at ~0.8s per decision — accuracy is not the deterministic selling point; reproducibility, auditability, and microsecond latency are.
The OpenAPPA replay CLI’s per-step cost scales superlinearly with trace length (measured 0.13s@50 → 2.3s@200 steps); per-step figures are quoted at the 40-step session scale.
methodology: Corpus: 40 deterministic scenarios engineered from the whitepaper’s threat taxonomy; T5/T6 are constructed to be detectable only with session-crossing state or content-side detection — they test the organ delta, not real-world prevalence.
Deterministic arms consume structured tool calls (their native interface); the LLM judge and regex arms consume the same scenarios as prose narratives (their native interface).
OpenAPPA arm: real v0.30.0 binary, replay mode, one .appa trace per session — the policy (9 tools) is written in OpenAPPA’s own idiom from their published examples and mirrored 1:1 in the TS arms.

Latency: TS arms measured in-process (hot loop, representative 6-decision mix); OpenAPPA measured as subprocess replay (includes startup; session-scale amortization); LLM judge wall-clock per call. These are not identical measurement modes — stated per arm, never averaged together.
Not comparable to the paper’s 1,320-eval Bench-Corp/ATB numbers: different corpus, different harness, single run.
